props.title: ulams — the open, AI-native LMS
props.description: Courses that stay true to their sources: an open-source, AI-native LMS with cited generation, a site per customer and standards built in.

props.title: Courses built from your docs. Every claim cited.
props.subtitle: AI drafts lessons from your material. You review every change before publishing.

props.title: Courses build much faster: a cited draft in minutes
props.text: In our own measured run, ULAMS turned a public docs repository into a 6-lesson course draft with 18 quiz questions, every block citing its source, in 7 min 44 s of generation.
props.statsLabel: One measured run · draft for author review

stats.label: minutes of generation (7 min 44 s)
stats.note: outline 24 s · lessons, quizzes, checks 6 min 57 s · apply 23 s

stats.label: hours of work per hour of finished course, built by hand

props.note: One run on one source, generation time only; author review comes on top. The two measure different things, so we claim no speed-up ratio.

props.title: Six academies, one platform
props.intro: Each demo is a separate tenant with its own theme, course and data, running on the same ulams install. Open it as a learner or step into its admin.
props.note: Demos reset every hour. No sign-up: you are logged in automatically.

props.title: Full analytics: see who is stuck, who finished and what to report
props.text: Per-course analytics, compliance reports and exports are built in, and the data stays in your own deployment.

props.title: Your brand, your subdomain: a white-label academy for every audience
props.text: Each academy is a tenant with its own subdomain, theme and data. Run one per client, department or audience, such as partners and employees, all on one ULAMS install.

bullets.title: A subdomain per academy
bullets.text: Each tenant gets its own host, database, storage bucket, keys and Redis prefix, so a token from one academy is rejected by every other.

bullets.title: Your look
bullets.text: Theme presets, an accent colour checked by a WCAG 2.2 AA contrast report that will not save a failing colour, and your logo with alt text.

bullets.title: Your identity on the web
bullets.text: A web manifest with the academy's name, theme colour and logo, and schema.org Course data on course pages.

bullets.title: Your messages and certificates
bullets.text: Each academy edits its own e-mail, SMS and PDF templates, certificates included, in its own database.

bullets.title: Sign-in per academy
bullets.text: Each academy can connect its own identity provider through SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect, next to Google and Facebook sign-in.

bullets.title: Storage per academy
bullets.text: With the bundled SeaweedFS store each academy gets its own S3 key, limited to its bucket.

props.note: One academy per subdomain today. A subdomain or entry point for each course or role inside one academy, with its own branding, is coming.

props.title: From one policy to certified, tracked training
props.intro: The path of a policy that has to be taught, passed and renewed, with what ships today and what is still coming.

items.title: A short interview becomes the course brief
items.text: The author answers questions about audience, duration, seniority and experience level, reviews the brief, and only then is the course drafted.

items.title: Your style guide shapes the course design
items.text: A brand import already turns a Figma file, a Stitch DESIGN.md or a brand guide into a theme you approve as a diff. Applying a style guide inside the course interview is coming.

items.title: Separate courses and academies per department
items.text: Separate academies per department work today. Creating them from one policy and keeping their courses linked is coming.

items.title: Lessons, a final test and a PDF certificate
items.text: Learners work through lessons, take a final test and download a PDF certificate with a public verification page.

items.title: Who completed required training
items.text: Required training with due dates, manager escalation, completion reports and an audit export. A policy-owner dashboard screen is coming.

items.title: Renewal when the policy changes
items.text: Certificates can expire and be recertified. Replacing them automatically after an approved policy change, with a new exam or course, is coming.

props.title: Knowledge grows when we build it together.
props.caption: Stanisław Ulam · illustrated portrait
paragraphs: In the cafés of Lwów, Stanisław Ulam and fellow mathematicians discussed problems and recorded them in a shared notebook: the Scottish Book. Questions, solutions and new ideas grew through collaboration.
Ulam later translated the collection so it could reach more people, inviting readers to contribute corrections and further developments.
props.connection: That spirit inspires ULAMS: turn your organisation’s documents into shared learning, work with people and agents, and keep improving the knowledge together. Open source, free to use and open to contribution.

source.label: The Scottish Book · Ulam’s preface, University of St Andrews

more.label: More questions on the FAQ page

items.a: ULAMS is an open-source LMS for organisations, universities and technical teams. Its headless API supports branded learning sites, course authoring and integrations.
Yes. ULAMS is MIT licensed. You provide hosting; paid AI provider calls, if enabled, are billed by your chosen provider. H5P runs as a separate service with its own GPL licence.

items.q: Can I try the whole stack locally?
items.a: Yes. Install the CLI and run ulams stack up with Docker Compose available. The development trial uses deterministic AI responses without paid model calls. Node.js 22.12 or newer is required.

Use Docker Compose on your own server or native Kubernetes manifests on an existing cluster. A VPS or virtual machine on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure can host the stack. Production needs DNS, HTTPS and persistent storage.
The CLI and MCP interface let compatible agents work with the platform. You can use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Gemini CLI, or integrate directly through the REST API.

items.q: Does AI publish a course automatically?
items.a: No. AI prepares a draft with source citations, and every AI change reaches you as a reviewable diff. The author reviews the outline and content, then approves publication. Production starts with AI disabled until you configure a provider.

items.q: Can each academy use its own brand and domain?
items.a: Yes. Each academy (tenant) has its own subdomain, learning site, theme, logo and isolated database, so you can run one per client, department or audience. The initial academy is created by the stack launcher; additional tenants use the platform tenant workflow. A subdomain for each course or role inside one academy is not built.

items.q: How do I stop it without losing courses?
items.a: Run ulams stack down. Data and credentials remain available when you run stack up again in the same installation directory. Only stack down --purge --yes deliberately removes persistent data.
